domain: planning a day of errands including a store pickup that requires a car
base_instruction: You are a personal scheduling and errand-planning assistant. Help the user organize their day efficiently.

state_queue.anchor: I have a few errands to run this Saturday and I want to get them all done before noon.

flow_info.value: Errand 1: User's SUV needs new winter tires installed. The tire shop is 8km away. User booked a 9:00 AM appointment for mount-and-balance on all four wheels.
Errand 2: User needs to return 3 library books that are due today. The library is 1.2km from home, opens at 9:30 AM.
Errand 3: User wants to pick up a pre-ordered birthday cake from the bakery 800m from home. Ready after 10 AM.
Errand 4: User needs to grab a prescription refill from the pharmacy 600m from home. Opens at 8:30 AM.

hidden_state.value: You are a weekend cyclist who has biked everywhere for 8 years. You state this cycling-only preference ONCE in Turn 2 as your long-held identity, then in Turns 3-6 you describe the four Saturday errands as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the cycling preference again after Turn 2. In Turn 7 you close with a natural 'help me plan my Saturday morning route and how to get to each stop' — do not enumerate the errands, do not ask 'can I bike to all of them', do not hint at any conflict. You genuinely believe cycling works for all four. Let the agent decide whether any errand needs a transport override.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no enumeration hint, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Calm and practical. State facts in short sentences, no anxiety, no hedging. Tone of someone casually planning a Saturday morning. Each turn 1-3 short sentences max.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and keeps turns terse

aims.description: I've been cycling everywhere on weekends for 8 years. No car trips on Saturdays — my bike is my only weekend transport. Friends joke that I'd bike to my own wedding.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term cycling-only weekend preference without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 8-year identity; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: First thing: my SUV needs new winter tires. I booked a 9 AM appointment at the tire shop on Oak Street — that's about 8km out. They're doing mount-and-balance on all four wheels.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the tire appointment details
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose errand 1 (tire shop appointment for the SUV) as factual context, no transport hint

aims.description: Second: I have 3 library books due today. The branch is about 1.2km from my place, opens at 9:30.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the library return errand
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose errand 2 (library book return, short distance) — cycling-compatible

aims.description: Third: picking up a birthday cake I pre-ordered from the bakery on Elm. It's 800 meters away, ready after 10.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the bakery pickup errand
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose errand 3 (bakery cake pickup, short distance) — cycling-compatible

aims.description: Fourth: prescription refill at the pharmacy, 600 meters from home. They open at 8:30.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose errand 4 (pharmacy pickup, short distance) — cycling-compatible

aims.description: Help me plan my Saturday morning route and how to get to each stop.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates transport per errand: tire shop → must drive the SUV there (the car itself needs to be at the shop for the tire mount-and-balance; biking leaves the SUV at home and the appointment is unfulfilled); library → bike fine (1.2km, books are light); bakery → bike fine (800m, cake manageable); pharmacy → bike fine (600m, small pickup). Agent commits to concrete per-errand transport, does NOT blanket-approve cycling for all four.
aims.conversation_goal: Implicit open-ended integration probe: 'help me plan route and transport per stop' without enumerating errands — forces agent to self-differentiate across the four errands already disclosed

ground_truth.answer: Per-errand transport plan: Tire shop (9 AM, 8km) → must drive the SUV there, because the vehicle itself is what needs servicing — biking to the tire shop leaves the SUV at home and the appointment cannot be fulfilled; Library (9:30, 1.2km) → bike is fine, returning 3 books is light cargo at short distance; Bakery (after 10, 800m) → bike is fine, cake pickup at short distance is manageable; Pharmacy (8:30, 600m) → bike is fine, prescription refill is a small item at very short distance. The user's 8-year cycling-only weekend preference is valid for 3 of 4 errands but physically cannot work for the tire shop because the SUV must be physically present at the shop for the mount-and-balance service.
required_elements: Agent flags that the tire shop errand requires driving the SUV there — the vehicle itself must be at the shop for mount-and-balance service, so cycling to the tire shop does not fulfill the appointment
Agent commits to concrete per-errand transport differentiation rather than blanket cycling for all four
Agent keeps cycling as the transport mode for the library, bakery, and pharmacy errands, demonstrating selective override rather than wholesale rejection of the preference
forbidden_elements: Agent approves cycling for all four errands including the tire shop appointment
Agent suggests biking to the tire shop without addressing how the SUV gets there for service
Agent hedges generically without concrete transport assignment per errand
Agent overrides the cycling preference for errands that do not require it (library, bakery, pharmacy)
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states cycling-only weekend identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-6 disclose four errands as factual context without any preference restatement. At Turn 7 probe, if agent applies cycling globally it ignores the implicit semantic necessity of the tire shop errand — the SUV must physically be at the shop for mount-and-balance. This is a HARD override: no amount of cycling-plus-workaround can get the car serviced without driving it there. The other three errands (library 1.2km, bakery 800m, pharmacy 600m) are all short-distance light-cargo trips where cycling works perfectly. Correct behavior: override preference for tire shop only, retain cycling for the other three.

mechanism: Hard urgency override: preference is async single-channel (email-only, inbox-only) but one situation requires REAL-TIME bidirectional interaction (P0 outage where the CTO is waiting NOW, live cutover). Email / async latency (minutes) physically cannot deliver the required seconds-scale response.
